classification.difficultyReason: Model triangle area with a quadratic, reject a negative length and use Pythagoras to find the hypotenuse.

content.prompt:
Use quadratic equations to solve the problem. Clearly define any pronumerals introduced into your solution.

In a right-angled triangle, one of the sides adjacent to the right angle is 4 cm longer than the other side. The area of the triangle is $48\text{ cm}^2$. Find the length of each of the three sides.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the shorter side adjacent to the right angle. The other adjacent side is $(x+4)$ cm.

$$\begin{align*}\frac12x(x+4)&=48\\x(x+4)&=96\\x^2+4x-96&=0\\(x-8)(x+12)&=0\end{align*}$$

By the null factor law, $x=8$ or $x=-12$. A length must be positive, so the adjacent sides are $8$ cm and $12$ cm.

Let $h$ cm be the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras:

$$\begin{align*}h^2&=8^2+12^2\\h^2&=208\\h&=\sqrt{208}\\h&=4\sqrt{13}\end{align*}$$

The three sides are $8\text{ cm}$, $12\text{ cm}$ and $4\sqrt{13}\text{ cm}$.
